methodology.Fees: Everything users pay the protocol: the price of every cat minted, the trading fee the hook takes on the $HASH pool, and the secondary-market royalty the collection routes to the hook. The mint price is derived per cat from the contract's own curve - the number of cats created so far times PRICE_STEP - rather than read from a transaction value, so a mint sent with excess ether cannot inflate it.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees. Every one of the three flows is paid by a user: the miner pays the entry price, the trader pays the swap fee, and the secondary-market buyer pays the royalty.
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus the rent paid out to living cats.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Rent paid to the cats already alive. Every mint splits its price between the cats that came before it and the hook; cat holders are suppliers whose asset earns, not holders of a governance token, so their cut is a cost of revenue. Measured as the mint price minus the hook's cut, which is exact and needs no reconstruction from the rent accumulator. The hook's cut is what it was owed in the window rather than what it was sent: a transfer that fails its gas stipend is held in the collection's hookDue and forwarded later, so the change in that balance is added back.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of revenue that joins the hook's buyback queue and is spent buying $HASH back on the pool and burning it. Measured at the fee source - the moment the hook receives and splits the money - rather than when a buyback executes, since the queue is drained gradually under a per-block cap.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The developer's share of revenue, at the hook's devBps rate, read from the chain rather than hardcoded.

Fees.Mint/Redeem Fees: The price paid for every cat mined in the window, derived per cat from the contract's price curve.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: The trading fee the hook takes on $HASH swaps. The pool's own fee is zero, so this is the whole of it. The rate decays from its opening value to its target over the first ten minutes of trading, so the amounts are read from FeeTaken rather than computed.
Fees.Creator Fees: Secondary-market royalties, which the collection routes to the hook as the ERC-2981 recipient - in ether, or in WETH when the sale settled in WETH.

UserFees.Mint/Redeem Fees: The price paid for every cat mined in the window.
UserFees.Token Swap Fees: The trading fee paid by swappers on the $HASH pool.

Revenue.Token Buy Back: The part of revenue that joins the buyback queue.
Revenue.Protocol Fees: The developer's share of revenue, at the hook's devBps rate.

SupplySideRevenue.Rent to Cat Holders: Rent accrued to the cats alive at the time of each mint, paid out of that mint's price.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: Ether queued for buying $HASH back on the pool and burning it.

ProtocolRevenue.Protocol Fees: The developer's share of everything the hook receives.

methodology.Volume: Completed swaps through every Route settlement generation (original engines, fee collectors and provider executors, builder integrations and the Route v2 executors: the October 1, 2026 executor, the flywheel executor route.fun and partners use since October 6, and the partner executor), counted once per trade, including integrations and treasury trades but excluding quotes, individual pool hops and swaps sent from or to wallet 0xd5d7c80c9f8ddd278526a2e46f0a57275fa6116d, which Route excludes from its own reported volume.
methodology.Fees: Actual Route swap fees (including builder-integration and Route v2 swaps), integrator fees on builder swaps, partner fees on partner-executor swaps, and ROUTE creator fees from its original bonding curve and Pons pool, excluding gas, other providers' fees, API subscriptions, private transfers and cross-chain fees.
methodology.Revenue: Swap fees and ROUTE creator fees earned by Route, counted once before buybacks and treasury spending; integrator fees paid to builders and partner fees paid to partners are excluded.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Tracked revenue less revenue-funded ROUTE buybacks, which may spend receipts from earlier days; LP funding is a separate capital allocation, not a revenue deduction.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Actual ETH input for early creator-revenue-funded dev-wallet purchases and completed automated ROUTE buybacks; excludes all LP budgets and purchases made for liquidity.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Integrator fees paid to builders on builder-integration swaps and partner fees paid to partners on partner-executor swaps. No other tracked fee receipt is paid to outside liquidity providers or referrers; LP funding is a subsequent capital allocation.

Fees.Swap Fees: Route fees paid on swaps through the tracked Route contracts, using the actual amount charged on each trade.
Fees.Builder Fees: Integrator fees charged on builder-integration swaps and paid directly to the builder.
Fees.Partner Fees: Partner fees charged on Route v2 partner-executor swaps and paid to the partner wallet (in USDG when converted in the swap), from the PartnerFee event.
Fees.Creator Fees: Actual creatorAmount distributed by ROUTE's bonding curve or original Pons pool, including the original dev wallet and every manager recipient; excludes the Pons protocol share.

Revenue.Swap Fees To Route: Swap fees received by Route before buybacks and treasury spending, including Route v2 fees paid directly to the treasury Safe or into the 60/5/35 revenue manager.
Revenue.Creator Fees To Route: ROUTE creator fees paid to its historical or current recipient; later escrow claims, fee conversions and internal transfers are not additional income.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Route: Swap fees collected by Route, before the separate deduction for completed buybacks.
ProtocolRevenue.Creator Fees To Route: ROUTE creator fees credited to Route, before the separate deduction for completed buybacks.
ProtocolRevenue.Token Buy Back: ETH spent buying ROUTE, deducted from protocol revenue when the purchase completes; spending earlier receipts can make this period's net amount negative.

SupplySideRevenue.Builder Fees: Integrator fees paid to builders on builder-integration swaps.
SupplySideRevenue.Partner Fees: Partner fees paid to partners on Route v2 partner-executor swaps.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: Actual ETH input for 100 post-launch dev-wallet buys funded by ROUTE creator fees (see the historical funding reconciliation) and completed buys from all four automated managers (the current Ramp manager splits revenue 60% buyback, 5% LP, 35% treasury); excludes the launch purchase, gas, and ROUTE bought within the separate capital-allocation budget.

methodology.Fees: Flat SOL fees paid by users to create a token, manage a token, create an OpenBook market and bulk send tokens on DexLab, received by the DexLab fee wallet on Solana.
methodology.Revenue: All fees (SOL paid by users to create a token, manage a token, create an OpenBook market and bulk send tokens on DexLab) are kept by DexLab. There is no supplier side and no token holder share.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All fees (SOL paid by users to create a token, manage a token, create an OpenBook market and bulk send tokens on DexLab) are kept by DexLab. There is no supplier side and no token holder share.

Fees.Protocol Fees: All flat SOL fees received by the DexLab fee wallet on Solana, retained entirely by the protocol.

Revenue.Protocol Fees: All flat SOL fees received by the DexLab fee wallet on Solana, retained entirely by the protocol.

ProtocolRevenue.Protocol Fees: All flat SOL fees received by the DexLab fee wallet on Solana, retained entirely by the protocol.

methodology.Fees: The 1% hook fee and the ~3.33% tax PonsV2MemeHook charges on every swap of the genesis SHROOM/MU pool, read from the hook's own sweep events and denominated in MU after the hook converts the SHROOM side. Neither rate is assumed: both come from the events, and the split between Pons and the creator is read from the hook at the block being priced.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees. The hook fee and the tax are charged to swappers.
methodology.Revenue: SHROOM token revenue only: MU allocated for holder dividends in pool-filtered sweeps, excluding Pons. This is not treasury revenue and includes no treasury LP earnings.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: MU allocated to all SHROOM holders from creatorAmount, recognized at the hook sweep. Actual recipient payments can occur later. Treasury holders are included in this token-wide allocation, so do not add treasury dividend receipts again.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 30% of the hook fee taken by Pons, the launchpad the token was issued through.

Fees.Hook Fee: The 1% fee PonsV2MemeHook charges on every swap of the genesis SHROOM/MU pool, recovered from the sweep by scaling Pons's cut up by its configured share.
Fees.Token Tax: The tax the hook charges alongside the fee, 3.33x it on every event to date. Taken as whatever the creator was swept beyond its share of the hook fee, so no rate is assumed.

Revenue.Hook Fee To SHROOM Holders: The creator's 70% of the hook fee, which reaches SHROOM holders through the MU dividend.
Revenue.Token Tax To SHROOM Holders: The tax, which reaches SHROOM holders through the MU dividend.

HoldersRevenue.Hook Fee To SHROOM Holders: The creator's 70% of the hook fee, allocated for SHROOM holders pro-rata in MU at the hook sweep; recipient payments may occur later.
HoldersRevenue.Token Tax To SHROOM Holders: The tax, allocated for SHROOM holders pro-rata in MU at the hook sweep; recipient payments may occur later.

SupplySideRevenue.Hook Fee To Pons: The 30% of the hook fee Pons takes as the launchpad, read from the hook's protocolFeeShareBps at the block being priced.

methodology.Fees: Treasury income only: earned fees from treasury-owned SHROOM LP positions plus actual MU dividend receipts. Token balances and returned LP principal are not income. All-holder SHROOM dividend allocations are reported separately in shroom.ts; do not sum the two scopes.
methodology.Revenue: Treasury income only: earned fees from treasury-owned SHROOM LP positions plus actual MU dividend receipts. Token balances and returned LP principal are not income. All-holder SHROOM dividend allocations are reported separately in shroom.ts; do not sum the two scopes.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Treasury income only: earned fees from treasury-owned SHROOM LP positions plus actual MU dividend receipts. Token balances and returned LP principal are not income. All-holder SHROOM dividend allocations are reported separately in shroom.ts; do not sum the two scopes.

Fees.LP Fees: Earned fees realized when a treasury-owned SHROOM Uniswap v4 position is modified, including collection, withdrawal, burn, and fees offset against new deposits. Read from the feesAccrued return value of PoolManager.modifyLiquidity in Allium's robinhood.raw.traces; principal is excluded. Ownership is reconstructed at the modification. The genesis hook pool is excluded.
Fees.MU Dividends: MU dividends actually received from the Pons distributor by the two confirmed treasury wallets, recognized on receipt. Excludes transfers to other holders, arbitrary MU deposits, and transfers between treasury wallets. Shared MU payouts do not encode which launch generated them.

Revenue.LP Fees To Treasury: Earned fees realized when a treasury-owned SHROOM Uniswap v4 position is modified, including collection, withdrawal, burn, and fees offset against new deposits. Read from the feesAccrued return value of PoolManager.modifyLiquidity in Allium's robinhood.raw.traces; principal is excluded. Ownership is reconstructed at the modification. The genesis hook pool is excluded.
Revenue.MU Dividends To Treasury: MU dividends actually received from the Pons distributor by the two confirmed treasury wallets, recognized on receipt. Excludes transfers to other holders, arbitrary MU deposits, and transfers between treasury wallets. Shared MU payouts do not encode which launch generated them.

ProtocolRevenue.LP Fees To Treasury: Earned fees realized when a treasury-owned SHROOM Uniswap v4 position is modified, including collection, withdrawal, burn, and fees offset against new deposits. Read from the feesAccrued return value of PoolManager.modifyLiquidity in Allium's robinhood.raw.traces; principal is excluded. Ownership is reconstructed at the modification. The genesis hook pool is excluded.
ProtocolRevenue.MU Dividends To Treasury: MU dividends actually received from the Pons distributor by the two confirmed treasury wallets, recognized on receipt. Excludes transfers to other holders, arbitrary MU deposits, and transfers between treasury wallets. Shared MU payouts do not encode which launch generated them.

methodology.Volume: USDC wagered: both stakes of every market at the moment they lock into escrow (a market is only created on-chain once fully matched). This is betting volume, not deposits — funding a balance is not counted, only money committed to a bet. Each dollar is counted exactly once: the two stakes come from two different bettors, so this is the pot, not the maker/taker double count an orderbook has to halve. Cancelled markets refund the stakes, but the matched notional stays counted, in line with other prediction markets.
methodology.Fees: Protocol fee plus judge fee, both charged on the pot when the winner claims.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol fee share of claims, paid to the protocol fee collector.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol fee share of claims, paid to the protocol fee collector.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Judge fees paid to the human judges who resolve bets.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Zero. There is no token.

Fees.Protocol fee on bet claim: Protocol fee taken from the pot when the winner claims (protocolFee on the Claimed event). The on-chain rate is 0 bps at launch, so this reads 0 until it is raised.
Fees.Judge fee on bet claim: Judge fee taken from the pot when the winner claims (arbiterFee on the Claimed event). Set per bet by the creator; 0 when the bet uses the house judge or names no fee.

Revenue.Protocol fee on bet claim: The protocol fee share, paid to the protocol fee collector.

SupplySideRevenue.Judge fee on bet claim: Judge fees paid to the human judges who resolve bets.

methodology.UserFees: Percentage of rewards paid to protocol
methodology.Fees: Commission charged by the validators kHYPE delegates to, on the staking rewards they produce for kHYPE.
methodology.Revenue: The half of that commission Kinetiq invoices back to each validator operator (invoice_rate_bps, 5000 to date).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: From 2026-04-09, 30% of the invoiced amount is kept by the treasury; it was 100% before.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The half of the commission the validator operators retain for running the nodes.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 70% of the invoiced amount, used to buy back KNTQ for sKNTQ holders from 2026-04-09.

Fees.Validator Commission: Validator commission on the staking rewards produced for kHYPE.

Revenue.Validator Commission Invoiced To Kinetiq: Commission invoiced back to validator operators by Kinetiq.

ProtocolRevenue.Validator Commission Invoiced To Kinetiq: From 2026-04-09, 30% of the invoiced commission is kept by the treasury; it was 100% before.

SupplySideRevenue.Validator Commission To Operators: Commission retained by the validator operators.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: 70% of the invoiced commission, used to buy back KNTQ for sKNTQ holders.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees paid in KNTQ on Hyperliquid spot, which is the side of a KNTQ trade the HIP-1 deployer's share applies to.
methodology.Revenue: All of the trading fees paid in KNTQ on Hyperliquid spot. deployerTradingFeeShare on KNTQ is 1.0, so the deployer keeps the whole KNTQ-denominated fee.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All of the trading fees paid in KNTQ on Hyperliquid spot. deployerTradingFeeShare on KNTQ is 1.0, so the deployer keeps the whole KNTQ-denominated fee.

Fees.KNTQ Spot Deployer Fees: Spot trading fees denominated in KNTQ.

Revenue.KNTQ Spot Deployer Fees: Retained in full by Kinetiq as the token's deployer.

ProtocolRevenue.KNTQ Spot Deployer Fees: Retained in full by Kinetiq as the token's deployer.

methodology.Fees: Curve mode: 1% base fee plus optional creator tax on every bonding-curve buy/sell, plus the flat (owner-adjustable, re-read live) launch fee, plus post-graduation Uniswap v4 pool fees realised at sweep. Instant-v4 mode: the 1% LP fee of SolonPad's own plain Uniswap v4 launch pools, realised when the permissionless FeeSplitter crank forwards it.
methodology.Revenue: Curve mode: the protocol's share of curve fees (per-token policy, read live) plus all launch fees. Instant-v4 mode: the ~50% of LP fees forwarded to the platform treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Curve mode: the creator and buyback-vault shares of curve fees, the full creator tax, and the creator/buyback share of post-graduation pool fees. Instant-v4 mode: the ~50% of LP fees forwarded to the launch creator's BeneficiaryVault position.

Fees.Curve Swap Fees: Base fee plus optional creator tax on every bonding-curve buy and sell (fee+tax fields of CurveBuy/CurveSell).
Fees.Launch Fees: Flat per-launch fee, re-read from the factory each window since it is owner-adjustable.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: Uniswap v4 pool fees on graduated curves, realised through the memeHook's PoolFeesSwept event.
Fees.Instant Launch Fees to Protocol: Protocol half of the 1% LP fee on SolonPad's plain (non-curve) v4 launch pools.
Fees.Instant Launch Fees to Creators: Creator half of the 1% LP fee on SolonPad's plain (non-curve) v4 launch pools.

Revenue.Curve Swap Fees to Protocol: Protocol's share of curve swap fees, per each token's live launch fee policy.
Revenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: Protocol's share of post-graduation pool fees, from PoolFeesSwept.
Revenue.Instant Launch Fees to Protocol: Protocol half of instant-v4 LP fees, from FeeSplitter.FeesForwarded.

ProtocolRevenue.Curve Swap Fees to Protocol: Protocol's share of curve swap fees, per each token's live launch fee policy.
ProtocolRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: Protocol's share of post-graduation pool fees, from PoolFeesSwept.
ProtocolRevenue.Instant Launch Fees to Protocol: Protocol half of instant-v4 LP fees, from FeeSplitter.FeesForwarded.

SupplySideRevenue.Curve Swap Fees to Creators: Creator's share of curve swap fees.
SupplySideRevenue.Curve Swap Fees to Meme Token Buybacks: Share of curve swap fees allocated to buyback and burn of the launched token.
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: The full optional creator tax on curve trades.
SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Creators: Creator's share of post-graduation pool fees.
SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Meme Token Buybacks: Buyback share of post-graduation pool fees.
SupplySideRevenue.Instant Launch Fees to Creators: Creator half of instant-v4 LP fees, paid into the launch's BeneficiaryVault position.

methodology.Fees: Everything traders pay copyfomo on every copied buy and sell (a 2% service fee plus the gas copyfomo fronts for them, billed back as one stablecoin transfer to the copyfomo treasury, counted on the day the fee is collected), plus the creator fees of the copyfomo token $COPY: the Pons launchpad hook takes 3% of every swap of the COPY/COIN pool on Robinhood Chain, of which 2.7% goes to the creator (1% hook fee, 70% to the creator, plus a 2% creator tax). Counted on the day of the trade, valued at the hourly COIN price. The fees are swept into COIN by Pons and claimed by copyfomo in batches later; the claims are not what is counted.
methodology.UserFees: The part paid by copyfomo users: service fee plus gas billed back. Excludes the $COPY creator fees, which are paid by $COPY traders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Referral rewards paid to copyfomo referrers, plus the actual on-chain cost copyfomo pays on users' behalf: the EVM bundler gas and the SOL spent by the Solana fee payer (transaction fees and token-account rent).
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus SupplySideRevenue, i.e. after the EVM bundler gas, the Solana fee payer cost and referral rewards: the service fee plus copyfomo's margin on gas, plus the $COPY creator fees (the 'token fees' figure on copyfomo.com/data). The 'protocol fees, after gas' figure on copyfomo.com/data is the service part before referral rewards.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Buyback & burn of $COPY, funded by the creator fees: what the copyfomo creator wallets pay (COIN or USDG) in every transaction where they buy $COPY from the pool and burn $COPY in the same transaction (the buyback account buys and burns in one user operation). Counted on the day of the buy, which follows the trades that generated the fees. A holder cashback leg (USDG distributed to $COPY holders) is planned and will be added when it goes live.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue minus HoldersRevenue: service revenue and the creator fees kept by copyfomo.

Fees.Treasury inflow: Every stablecoin transfer into the copyfomo treasury. The service fee and the gas billed back to the trader arrive together in one transfer and cannot be split on-chain.
Fees.$COPY creator fees: 2.7% of the COIN leg of every swap of the COPY/COIN Uniswap v4 pool on Robinhood Chain (PoolManager Swap events of the pool), valued at the hourly COIN price on Dune. Rate from the hook's launch config: 1% hook fee with 70% to the creator, plus a 2% creator tax.

UserFees.Treasury inflow: Same as the Fees component: everything copyfomo users pay.

SupplySideRevenue.Referral rewards: USDC sent by the copyfomo referral payout wallet on Base to referrers (its top-ups from the treasury are internal and excluded), plus any stablecoin sent by the treasury back to identified copyfomo user wallets.
SupplySideRevenue.Bundler gas cost: Gas the copyfomo bundler wallets paid to the ERC-4337 EntryPoint for users' operations, priced with the daily WETH / WBNB price.
SupplySideRevenue.Solana fee payer cost: SOL spent by the copyfomo Solana fee payer, which signs every copyfomo Solana transaction: signature fees and the rent of the token accounts it creates, net of rent returned on close (its balance change in its own transactions, excluding its top-ups co-signed by the Solana treasury), priced with the daily SOL price.

HoldersRevenue.Buyback & burn: COIN and USDG sent by the copyfomo creator wallets in every transaction that swaps on the COPY/COIN pool, delivers $COPY to them and burns $COPY from them (Transfer to the zero address) in that same transaction, since 2026-09-11 when the buyback programme started. The three manual buys of 2026-09-11, burned the next day in one transaction (hash in the query helper), are listed explicitly.

Revenue.Treasury inflow: Same as the Fees component: gross service fees before the supply-side deductions.
Revenue.$COPY creator fees: Same as the Fees component: creator fees have no supply-side share.
Revenue.Referral rewards: Same as the SupplySideRevenue component, subtracted from gross fees.
Revenue.Bundler gas cost: Same as the SupplySideRevenue component, subtracted from gross fees.
Revenue.Solana fee payer cost: Same as the SupplySideRevenue component, subtracted from gross fees.

ProtocolRevenue.Buyback & burn: Same as the HoldersRevenue component, subtracted from Revenue.

methodology.Fees: Actual MON fees accrued to the protocol treasury and sent to the buyback vault at round settlement, plus separately paid auto-bet gas subsidies. Excludes MON allocated back to players and does not count gross stakes as fees.
methodology.Revenue: MON round settlement fees retained by the treasury and buyback vault; excludes auto-bet execution fees paid to the gas-subsidy wallet.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: User-paid auto-bet execution fees transferred to the execution wallet as gas subsidies, included in Fees but excluded from Revenue; measures the subsidy paid, not actual transaction gas expenditure.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: MON round fees allocated directly to the protocol treasury; excludes gas subsidies, the separate buyback budget and GONE inventory valuations.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Successful GONE staking rewards funded by the buyback vault, valued in MON at the matching buyback's actual execution rate (MON spent / GONE bought), then priced in USD by the SDK. Includes pending rewards only when successfully funded; excludes mining allocations, no-staker treasury diversions, other funders and later claims. Execution-price valuation includes trading costs and is not an independent GONE market price.

Fees.Round Fees To Treasury: Actual MON accrued to the round treasury in ProtocolTreasuryAccrued.amount.
Fees.Round Fees To Buyback Vault: Actual MON sent to the buyback vault in BuybackFeeDistributed.amount, including the remaining pot when no winning stake exists.
Fees.Auto-Bet Execution Fees: The fee field of each successful AutoBetExecuted event.

Revenue.Round Fees To Treasury: Actual MON accrued to the round treasury in ProtocolTreasuryAccrued.amount.
Revenue.Round Fees To Buyback Vault: Actual MON sent to the buyback vault in BuybackFeeDistributed.amount, including the remaining pot when no winning stake exists.

SupplySideRevenue.Auto-Bet Execution Fees: The fee field of each successful AutoBetExecuted event, paid to the auto-bet execution wallet as a gas subsidy.

ProtocolRevenue.Round Fees To Treasury: Actual MON accrued to the round treasury in ProtocolTreasuryAccrued.amount.

HoldersRevenue.GONE Staking Rewards At Buyback Executio: RewardFunded.amount from the buyback vault multiplied by the matching BuybackExecuted.monAmount / goneAmount. Match by transaction and log order; round down to MON wei per funding event. Pending rewards use the successful funding transaction's rate.

methodology.Fees: USDC-side Uniswap V3 swap fees accrued on Tolly's locked launch pools. Excludes the project-token-side fee leg, which is burned outright but has no reliable USD price.
methodology.Revenue: The 10% protocol-treasury share plus the 9% spent buying and burning TOLLY.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 10% share paid to the treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 9% share market-bought back into TOLLY and burned.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 64% creator share, the 12% launched-token holder-reward share, and the 5% that buys and burns the launched token itself.

Fees.Trading Fees: USDC-denominated Uniswap V3 swap fees accrued on a Tolly launch pool.

Revenue.Trading Fees to Protocol Treasury: 10% of collected fees, paid to the treasury.
Revenue.Trading Fees to TOLLY Buyback: 9% of collected fees, spent buying and burning TOLLY.

ProtocolRevenue.Trading Fees to Protocol Treasury: 10% of collected fees, paid to the treasury.

HoldersRevenue.Trading Fees to TOLLY Buyback: 9% of collected fees, market-bought back into TOLLY and burned.

SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees to Creators: 64% (the remainder) of collected fees, paid to the token's creator.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees to Launched Token Holders: 12% of collected fees, booked to the launched token's holder-reward vault.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees to Project Token Buyback: 5% of collected fees, spent buying back and burning the launched token.

methodology.Fees: The fee a V5 or V6 launch pool charges on each trade, taken by that launch's hook inside the swap itself and read from the hook's own event, so the rate is never assumed here. It is 1% at regime; an anti-sniper launch charges more on buys during its opening window, on a curve that decays over the first blocks - 95%, then 70%, 40% and 10% - before settling at the same 1%, while sells in that window pay the regime rate. The fee is taken in either the launched token or its quote asset, whichever side the trader paid in. Both generations are read: V6 only took over new launches, it did not stop V5's existing pools from trading. V1-V4 legacy launches (pre-hook, plain Uniswap v3 with a per-launch lock contract) are not covered.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Everything not kept by the protocol: the creator's share, the remainder streamed to the launched token's own holders via the Reward Vault on Holder-Rewards launches, and - on fees taken during the opening window - the 80% earmarked to the launch's Treasury Reserve, which buys the launched token back to burn it.

Fees.Launch Pool Fees: Fee withheld by a V5 or V6 launch hook on each trade in that launch's Uniswap v4 pool - 1% at regime, and up to 95% on buys in the first blocks of an anti-sniper launch's opening window - in whichever currency (launched token or quote asset) the trader paid in.

Revenue.Launch Pool Fees to Protocol: Protocol's share of each fee: 50% by default, 30% on Holder-Rewards launches, 10% during a launch's opening window.

ProtocolRevenue.Launch Pool Fees to Protocol: Protocol's share of each fee: 50% by default, 30% on Holder-Rewards launches, 10% during a launch's opening window.

SupplySideRevenue.Launch Pool Fees to Creators: Creator's share of each fee: 50% by default, 30% on Holder-Rewards launches, 10% during a launch's opening window.
SupplySideRevenue.Launch Pool Fees to Token Holders: Holder-Rewards launches only: the ~40% remainder streamed to the launched token's own holders via the Reward Vault.
SupplySideRevenue.Launch Pool Fees to Token Buyback: Opening-window fees only: the 80% remainder sent to the launch's Treasury Reserve, which bids under the price to buy the launched token back and burn it.

methodology.Fees: The full USDC mint-settlement price paid by miners for every ArcLotls organism, read from the three downstream shares (rent, treasury, buyback) the mint payment is split into on-chain, which always sum to 100% of the mint price. Excludes the LOTL opening-trade tax (a one-time anti-snipe launch mechanic) and any undocumented trading-fee revenue not yet observed on-chain.
methodology.Revenue: Mint fees minus the share paid out as rent to NFT holders: the treasury share plus the share earmarked for the LOTL buyback-and-burn reserve.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury share of every mint (25% as observed on-chain).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rent share of every mint (60% as observed on-chain), paid out to NFT holders weighted by organism stage. Accrued when funded, not when claimed.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of every mint earmarked for buying LOTL back and burning it (15% as observed on-chain), measured at the fee source (when USDC lands in the buyback reserve) rather than at execution.

Fees.Mint Fees: USDC paid by miners to mint an ArcLotls organism, summed across its three downstream shares (rent, treasury, buyback).

Revenue.LOTL Token Buy Back: Share of mint fees earmarked for the LOTL buyback-and-burn reserve.

SupplySideRevenue.Mint Fees To Rent Pool: Rent share of mint fees, paid to NFT holders.

HoldersRevenue.LOTL Token Buy Back: USDC earmarked for buying LOTL back and burning it, measured when it is funded rather than when the buyback executes.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees collected by vibes.fun: the 1% platform fee on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a coin graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Key vibes.fun holds. Raydium's own protocol fee is excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token.
methodology.UserFees: Same as fees, paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: 30% of fees: the share vibes.fun keeps, split between its treasury and $VIBES buyback and burn.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 15% of fees, sent to the vibes.fun treasury (Squads multisig).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: 15% of fees, used to buy back and burn $VIBES.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 70% of fees, paid to the holders of the coin that generated them, or to its creator when the creator chose creator fees.

Fees.Trading Fees: 1% of every LaunchLab bonding curve trade on a vibes.fun launch, charged in the pool's quote token.
Fees.LP Fees: Quote-token fees harvested from the locked liquidity of graduated vibes.fun launches.

Revenue.Trading Fees: 30% of bonding curve platform fees, kept by vibes.fun.
Revenue.LP Fees: 30% of harvested locked liquidity fees, kept by vibes.fun.

ProtocolRevenue.Trading Fees: 15% of bonding curve platform fees, sent to the treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.LP Fees: 15% of harvested locked liquidity fees, sent to the treasury.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: 15% of fees spent buying $VIBES back and burning it.

SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees: 70% of bonding curve platform fees, paid to the holders of the coin that generated them or to its creator.
SupplySideRevenue.LP Fees: 70% of harvested locked liquidity fees, paid to the holders of the coin or to its creator.

methodology.Fees: All REP369 transaction tax paid by users. The adapter reads fee-component settings from the REP369 contract and applies on-chain fee-update events in chronological order.
methodology.Revenue: REP369 tax allocated to REP holder rewards plus the sell-side burn allocation. Automatic liquidity is treated as supply-side revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: No separate protocol treasury fee is present in the current REP369 fee configuration.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: REP rewards plus the REP369 sell-side burn allocation.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The portion of REP369 transaction tax allocated to automatic liquidity.

Fees.REP369 Transaction Tax: Exact REP369 tax transfers associated with user-facing swaps on the main REP369/WPLS pair, including the direct sell-side burn transfer.

Revenue.REP Rewards: REP369 tax allocated to the REP reward mechanism for holders.
Revenue.Token Burns: REP369 sell-tax portion sent to the ERC-20 zero address by the token contract.

HoldersRevenue.REP Rewards: The REP369 tax component allocated to holder rewards.
HoldersRevenue.Token Burns: The REP369 sell-tax component permanently burned by the token contract.

SupplySideRevenue.Auto Liquidity: The REP369 tax component allocated to automatic liquidity.

methodology.Fees: All trading fees settled into FociFeeEscrow during the day (curve fees, creator tax, converted post-graduation hook fees, curve referral fees), plus hook referral fees claimed that day. Recognised when swept by the keeper, not when traded.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every fee is paid by traders on buys and sells.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol fee recipient's share plus the share paid to holder-reward distributors.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Escrow credits to the protocol fee recipient (the protocol's frozen share of each launch's trading fee).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Escrow credits to FociRewardsDistributor contracts — launches that elected to pay their creator share to token holders.

methodology.Fees: LP fees earned by the listed TickerSpring V7 vaults during the UTC day, including uncollected fees. Measured as the change in cumulative harvested plus pending native-token fees from saved on-chain observations. Excludes principal, stock-price returns, retired vaults and lending.
methodology.Revenue: Earned vault LP fees allocated to operations (10%) and the SPRING buyback reserve (20%), subject to raw-token rounding.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The operations allocation of earned vault LP fees (10%).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The allocation reserved to buy and permanently burn SPRING (20%), measured when vault fees accrue rather than when the buyback executes.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Earned LP fees retained for vault depositors after protocol allocations (approximately 70%).

Fees.Vault Liquidity Fees: Daily change in grossFees plus position.pendingFees, in each underlying token, from the public daily history API. Harvesting moves fees between these counters without counting them twice. Missing observations fail instead of returning zero.

Revenue.Vault Fees To Operations: The operations allocation of earned vault LP fees (10%).
Revenue.Vault Fees To Buyback Reserve: The allocation reserved for future SPRING buybacks and burns (20%), measured when fees accrue rather than when the buyback executes.

ProtocolRevenue.Vault Fees To Operations: The operations allocation of earned vault LP fees (10%).

HoldersRevenue.Vault Fees To Buyback Reserve: The allocation reserved for future SPRING buybacks and burns (20%), measured when fees accrue rather than when the buyback executes.

SupplySideRevenue.Vault Fees To Depositors: Earned vault LP fees minus the accrued operations and buyback-reserve allocations.

methodology.Fees: The tax ArgusPad's per-launch hook charges on every buy and sell, the trading fee each launch's pool charges (on Portals 3-7 the 1% pool fee earned by the permanently locked launch position; on Portal 8 a 1% base fee the hook charges in the quote asset in its place), and the extra tax charged on buys in a launch's first seconds. Counted in the asset the fee is charged in, at the moment it is charged, so the protocol's later sale of the launched tokens it was paid is not counted a second time. Fees charged in the launched token itself (Portals 3-7 only; Portal 8 takes every fee in the quote asset) are reported in that token's own units and are priced only if DefiLlama has a price for it; it has none for these tokens today, because a launched token's only market is the pool ArgusPad seeded, and pricing it there overstates by about 40% against what ArgusPad's own sales of them actually realise.
methodology.Revenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the fees, which leave the protocol divided at the weights each launch fixed at creation: the token creator's share, the dividends paid to holders of that launched token, the share added back into the launch's permanently locked liquidity, the share used to buy and burn the launched token, and on Portal 8 the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently.

Fees.Swap Tax: The launch's own buy and sell tax, chosen per launch (1-10%), taken by its hook on each swap: on Portals 3-7 read from that swap's TaxTaken, net of the tax the splitter pays itself when it sells launched tokens through the launch's own pool, which is not paid by any user; on Portal 8 the tax part of QuoteFeeTaken's bucketFee. The hook charges it outside the pool fee, so it is not inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc.
Fees.LP Fees: Portals 3-7: the 1% Uniswap v4 pool fee earned by the launch's permanently locked position, read as what the locker forwarded to the splitter, net of the position principal that comes back through the same call. These fees are also inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: Portal 8: the 1% base fee the hook adds to every buy and sell and takes in the quote asset. Portal 8 pools are dynamic-fee pools whose pool fee is set to zero on every swap, so this replaces the LP fee and goes to the same split; it is not inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc. It is the base's proportional part of QuoteFeeTaken's bucketFee, which prices tax and base as one rate.
Fees.Snipe Tax: An extra, time-decaying tax on buys in the seconds after a launch opens, charged by the same hook and paid directly to the treasury (Portal 8: QuoteFeeTaken's surcharge).

Revenue.Swap Fees to Treasury: treasuryBps of each launch's accrued fee, read from that launch's own splitter or escrow (1000 on every Portal 3-7 launch, 3000 on every Portal 8 launch), plus the whole snipe tax, which the hook pays straight to the treasury without passing through a splitter, plus on Portal 8 any holders' share accrued while no holder was eligible, which the hook also pays straight to the treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees to Treasury: treasuryBps of each launch's accrued fee, read from that launch's own splitter or escrow (1000 on every Portal 3-7 launch, 3000 on every Portal 8 launch), plus the whole snipe tax, which the hook pays straight to the treasury without passing through a splitter, plus on Portal 8 any holders' share accrued while no holder was eligible, which the hook also pays straight to the treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: The token creator's share, at that launch's configured creatorBps, credited to the creator to claim. Takes the remainder of the supply side, so fees equal revenue plus supply-side revenue exactly.
SupplySideRevenue.Launched Token Holder Dividends: Dividends paid out to holders of the launched token, at that launch's configured dividendBps. These are not ARGUS holders, so they are a supply-side cost rather than holders revenue.
SupplySideRevenue.Fees Compounded Into Locked Liquidity: The share added straight back into the launch's permanently locked position instead of being paid to anyone, at that launch's configured liquidityBps.
SupplySideRevenue.Launched Token Buy and Burn: The share used to buy and burn the launched token, at that launch's configured burnBps. It buys the launched token, not ARGUS, so it is a cost carried by that launch's supply side rather than a protocol buyback or a payment to holders.
SupplySideRevenue.Launched Token Buy and Lock: Portal 8: the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently in the line's lock vault, at that launch's configured lockBps. Like the burn it buys the launched token, not ARGUS, so it is supply side.

methodology.Fees: What users pay to cross the bridge. The asset's controller on Arc charges the same rate in both directions - on the way in it mints the fee to the protocol and the rest to the user, on the way out it burns the gross and re-mints the fee - and an optional fast-lane router charges its own cut on top for skipping the queue, on the origin chain when depositing and on Arc when redeeming. Anything charged on Arc is taken in the claim token (bCRCL, bGLD, bUSDT, bBTCB), which is a 1:1 claim on the asset held in custody and is therefore valued as that origin asset; a fast-lane deposit is charged on the origin chain instead, before the asset becomes a claim, so it is taken in the origin token directly. Either way the fee is denominated in the same four origin assets.
methodology.Revenue: All the bridge fees and the fast-lane fees go to the protocol's treasury with nothing paid out of it.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All the bridge fees and the fast-lane fees go to the protocol's treasury with nothing paid out of it.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders on every swap.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders, taken from each Swap event's swapFeeAmount. The Vault charges the fee on the input token; it is booked on the same leg as the volume. When that leg is the output token (a non-core token sold for a core asset), the fee is converted at the trade's own rate, amountOut * swapFeeAmount / amountIn - no external price is used. The amount is exact; only its denomination changes. Because amountIn includes the fee itself and the trade's average rate is slightly worse than the pool's marginal rate, the converted fee reads low by about the pool's fee rate plus the trade's own price impact - a share of the fee, never of volume, and always in the under-counting direction.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of the swap fee, read per pool from the protocol fee controller.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue - the protocol's share of the swap fee goes to the protocol fee controller.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Zero - no part of the fee is distributed to token holders today.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the swap fee: the part that stays in the pool for liquidity providers, plus the pool creator's share when a pool creator has set one.
methodology.Volume: Value swapped through the Ranges Vault, counted once per trade from the core asset leg when the trade has one, otherwise from the token sold into the pool.

breakdownMethodology.Volume: Value swapped through the Ranges Vault, counted once per trade.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees charged by the Vault on every trade (swapFeeAmount). The Vault denominates the fee in the input token; it is booked on the same leg as the volume, converted at the trade's own rate when that leg is the output token.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees paid by traders on every trade.

Revenue.Protocol Fees: Protocol's share of the swap fee, per pool.

ProtocolRevenue.Protocol Fees: Protocol's share of the swap fee, per pool.

SupplySideRevenue.LP Fees: Share of the swap fee left in the pool for liquidity providers.
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: Pool creator's share of the swap fee, set per pool by its creator.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: what the trader paid on each swap.
methodology.Fees: Two things the trader pays. The pool fee on each swap - two of these pools run Ellipse's market-hours hook and charge 1%, 2% or 3% depending on whether the underlying market is open or shut, so for those the rate is read from the swap itself rather than assumed, and the rest are fixed at creation. Plus Ellipse's own 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, read from the event its fee collector emits when it is emptied, which reports what actually reached the treasury rather than what was sent.
methodology.Revenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The pool fee, which goes to the liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume in Ellipse's own markets on Arc: the Uniswap pools it opened for the assets it bridges (bCRCL, bGLD, bBTCB, bUSDT) and the market for its own token. Each swap is counted once, on whichever side has a price - USDC everywhere except the ELLIPSE market, which is counted on its bCRCL side and valued as the CRCL held in custody behind it. Launchpad launches are not counted: those pools are opened for other people's tokens on Uniswap's shared PoolManager, so their volume belongs to that DEX.

Fees.Swap Fees: Fee paid to the pool on each swap.
Fees.Interface Fees: Ellipse's 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, read from its fee collector's event.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees: The pool fee, which goes to the liquidity providers.

Revenue.Interface Fees: Ellipse's 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, kept in full.

ProtocolRevenue.Interface Fees: Ellipse's 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, kept in full.

methodology.Volume: ETH paid by purchasers for pulls.
methodology.Fees: Acquisition fees net of quick-sell payouts, plus settlement fees, retained penalties and early crown exit fees.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol's cut of fees after builder rewards, kept by the team or spent on burned FWA.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol's cut of fees paid to the team.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: FWA bought back with protocol fees and burned.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees paid to NFT depositors, builder rewards, and the FWA rewards and caller incentive paid from buybacks.

Fees.Acquisition Fees: ETH paid by purchasers for pulls, net of payouts to purchasers who sell the NFT back.
Fees.Settlement Fees: 1% of the listing backing when the purchaser keeps or relists the NFT.
Fees.Retained Settlement Penalties: Part of the listing backing kept when a purchaser sells the NFT back.
Fees.Early Crown Exit Fees: 1% of the backing when the top listing is withdrawn or reduced within 12 hours.

Revenue.Acquisition Fees: Protocol's cut of acquisition fees kept by the team or spent on burned FWA.
Revenue.Settlement Fees: Settlement fees kept by the team or spent on burned FWA.
Revenue.Retained Settlement Penalties: Retained penalties kept by the team or spent on burned FWA.
Revenue.Early Crown Exit Fees: Early crown exit fees kept by the team or spent on burned FWA.

SupplySideRevenue.Acquisition Fees: Acquisition fees paid to NFT depositors.
SupplySideRevenue.Top Listing Reward: Acquisition fees paid to the top-backed listing.
SupplySideRevenue.Builder Rewards: Share of protocol fees paid to third parties that submit pulls for purchasers.
SupplySideRevenue.FWA Rewards To Depositors: FWA from buybacks paid to depositors.
SupplySideRevenue.FWA Rewards To Purchasers: FWA from buybacks paid to purchasers.
SupplySideRevenue.Buyback Caller Incentive: ETH paid to whoever runs a buyback.

ProtocolRevenue.Acquisition Fees: Team share of the protocol's cut of acquisition fees.
ProtocolRevenue.Early Crown Exit Fees: Team share of early crown exit fees.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back And Burn: FWA bought back with protocol fees and burned.

methodology.Fees: The 0.25% integrator fee HyperDex charges on every swap, bridge and basket order routed through LI.FI: the FeesForwarded leg paid to HyperDex in a transaction whose LI.FI event carries integrator "hyperdex".
methodology.Revenue: All of the integrator fee goes to HyperDex.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All of the integrator fee goes to HyperDex.

Fees.Integrator fee: The 0.25% integrator fee paid to HyperDex on each LI.FI-routed order.

Revenue.Integrator fee: The 0.25% integrator fee paid to HyperDex on each LI.FI-routed order.

ProtocolRevenue.Integrator fee: The 0.25% integrator fee paid to HyperDex on each LI.FI-routed order.

methodology.Fees: The full native-USDC entry price accepted for every BoneYard NFT mint, read from Boneyard's Minted.price event. Excludes BONE genesis reserve, BONE emitted by burns, secondary royalties, and hook swap levies.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every included amount is paid by a miner in a successful Boneyard mint.
methodology.Revenue: Mint fees less Charge paid to existing Skeletons. Before LP activation, the retained revenue is the project share plus protocol-owned liquidity bootstrap; after LP activation it is the project share plus BONE-buyback funding.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Charge accrued to active Skeleton holders from mint #9 onward (65% under the deployed constant). Charge is measured when it accrues, not when a holder later claims or burns.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The project slice emitted by Hook.ProjectShareAdded plus the pre-LP bootstrap retained by Boneyard to seed its canonical protocol-owned liquidity. If seedLiquidity diverts bootstrap that cannot be paired with BONE into the Hook buyback reserve, that previously booked protocol revenue is reclassified out on BootstrapDivertedToBuyback. Hook-bound revenue is 100% of each of the first eight genesis mints and 35% of later mints.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Native USDC allocated by Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded from post-LP mints for market-buying and burning BONE, plus any pre-LP bootstrap reclassified to that reserve by BootstrapDivertedToBuyback at liquidity seeding. It is counted when funded, not when the owner executes the capped buyback. BONE is the protocol's own value-accrual token.

Fees.Boneyard Mint Fees: The exact price field from each successful Boneyard Minted event.

Revenue.Mint Fees To Project: Project share emitted by the Hook for a successful mint.
Revenue.Mint Fees To Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bo: Pre-LP mint share retained by Boneyard and later committed to its canonical protocol-owned liquidity position.
Revenue.BONE Buyback Reserve: Post-LP mint share credited to the BONE buyback-and-burn reserve.
Revenue.Mint Rounding Remainder Retained In Bone: Native wei left in Boneyard by Solidity's independent integer floors for Charge and the hook share; it is not a project payout or BONE buyback allocation.

SupplySideRevenue.Mint Fees To Skeleton Charge: Charge accrued to Skeletons alive before each post-genesis mint; holder claims and burn-time Charge payouts are settlement of this already-counted accrual.

ProtocolRevenue.Mint Fees To Project: The project portion of hook-bound mint revenue, taken from Hook.ProjectShareAdded.
ProtocolRevenue.Mint Fees To Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bo: Pre-LP mint share retained by Boneyard and later committed to its canonical protocol-owned liquidity position.
ProtocolRevenue.Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bootstrap Recla: Negative protocol-revenue reclassification when seedLiquidity diverts an already-booked bootstrap remainder into the Hook's BONE buyback reserve.
ProtocolRevenue.Mint Rounding Remainder Retained In Bone: Native wei retained by Boneyard from Solidity's independent integer floors for Charge and the hook share.

HoldersRevenue.BONE Buyback Reserve: Post-LP mint funding for BONE market buybacks and burns, read from Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded and excluding seed-time bootstrap diversion.
HoldersRevenue.Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bootstrap Recla: Bootstrap previously classified as protocol-owned liquidity that seedLiquidity explicitly diverts to the BONE buyback-and-burn reserve.

methodology.Fees: Commission paid by limit-order makers (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn) plus the Uniswap v4 LP fees earned by resting order liquidity, booked when an order is settled or partially filled at creation. Amounts in other tokens are valued on the USDG side at the order band's own execution price.
methodology.Revenue: All commission (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All commission (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LP fees earned by order liquidity, net of commission, credited to order makers.

Fees.Limit Order Commission: Commission on the proceeds of filled orders, including partial fills at creation (2.5%, snapshotted per order).
Fees.Limit Order LP Fees: Uniswap v4 LP fees earned by resting order liquidity while the pool price moved through its band.

Revenue.Limit Order Commission To Treasury: Commission on order proceeds, paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
Revenue.Limit Order LP Fees To Treasury: Commission on LP fees earned by orders (2.5%), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Limit Order Commission To Treasury: Commission on order proceeds, paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.Limit Order LP Fees To Treasury: Commission on LP fees earned by orders (2.5%), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Limit Order LP Fees To Order Makers: LP fees earned by orders minus commission, credited to order makers.

methodology.Fees: Everything users pay through Packed: the flat 0.0004 ETH launch fee, the 1% fee on every trade on a Packed bonding curve (Robinhood Chain), the 1% LP fee of every Packed coin's Uniswap v4 pool (after graduation on Robinhood Chain, from launch on Ethereum), the creator tax a coin's creator sets at launch (0-5%, on curve trades and pool swaps), the anti-snipe charges of a coin's first seconds or first block, and the bids paid for seats in packs launched from deposits on Ethereum. All of it is paid by users: launch fees and bids by creators and pack members, the rest by traders. Pool fees are counted when they are collected from the position.
methodology.Revenue: Packed's share: the launch fee in full, 25% of the 1% curve fee, 25% of the 1% pool fee, and half of every seat bid.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue minus the ETH spent buying back $PACKD, which is moved to HoldersRevenue. Negative on days when a buyback spends more than that day's revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator's 75% of the 1% curve and pool fees, the whole creator tax and anti-snipe charges, and the launcher's half of seat bids. For a reward coin the creator's share goes to the coin's holders instead.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: ETH Packed spends buying back $PACKD, its own token, on the open market on Robinhood Chain, from the fee wallet and the team wallet; the coins bought are burned. It is part of Revenue, moved out of ProtocolRevenue.

Fees.Launch Fees: Flat 0.0004 ETH paid by the creator for each coin launched.
Fees.Curve Trading Fees: 1% of the quote side of every buy and sell on a Packed bonding curve on Robinhood Chain.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: The 1% LP fee of a Packed coin's Uniswap v4 pool, in both currencies, counted when collectFees takes it out of the position.
Fees.Creator Tax: The creator's own tax (0-5%, fixed at launch) on curve trades and pool swaps, including the decaying anti-snipe tax of a Robinhood curve's first seconds.
Fees.Launch Block Surcharge: The surcharge on buys in an Ethereum coin's launch block, other than the launch's own buys.
Fees.Pack Seat Bids: Bids paid by pack members for their seats in packs launched from deposits on Ethereum.

Revenue.Launch Fees to Protocol: The launch fee, kept in full by Packed.
Revenue.Pack Seat Bids to Protocol: Half of every seat bid, paid to Packed by the factory inside the launch.

ProtocolRevenue.Launch Fees to Protocol: The launch fee, kept in full by Packed.
ProtocolRevenue.Pack Seat Bids to Protocol: Half of every seat bid, paid to Packed by the factory inside the launch.
ProtocolRevenue.Token Buy Back: Same as the HoldersRevenue component, subtracted from protocol revenue.

SupplySideRevenue.Curve Trading Fees to Creators: The creator's 75% of the 1% curve fee (the coin's holders' for a reward coin).
SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Creators: The creator's 75% of the 1% pool fee (the coin's holders' for a reward coin).
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Tax: The creator tax and the curve's anti-snipe tax, all of it the creator's (the holders' for a reward coin).
SupplySideRevenue.Launch Block Surcharge: The Ethereum launch-block surcharge, paid to the creator.
SupplySideRevenue.Pack Seat Bids to Launchers: The launcher's half of every seat bid.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: ETH spent by the fee wallet and the team wallet swapping for $PACKD in the ETH/$PACKD Uniswap v4 pool, on the day of each buy. The coins bought are burned.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees directly paid by traders.
methodology.Fees: V2 swap fees paid by traders, taken from each pool's Fees events, which record the exact fee charged on each swap's input amount at the fee rate in effect for that swap.
methodology.Revenue: V2 swap fees routed to veArchery voters through gauges, equal to HoldersRevenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees accrued to the gauge's staked LP balance, from the pool's fee index accounting: change in claimable + balanceOf(gauge) * (index - supplyIndex[gauge]) / 1e18, plus fees the gauge claimed in the period.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: V2 liquidity provider fees not routed to veArchery voters.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume from Archery v2 pools on Arc. Each swap is counted once on the pricing side of the pair.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: All v2 swap fees paid by traders.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: All v2 swap fees paid directly by traders.

Revenue.V2 Gauge Voter Fees: V2 pool swap fees accrued to LP tokens staked in gauges and routed to veArchery voters.

HoldersRevenue.V2 Gauge Voter Fees: V2 pool swap fees accrued to LP tokens staked in gauges and routed to veArchery voters.

SupplySideRevenue.V2 Liquidity Provider Fees: V2 pool swap fees retained by unstaked liquidity providers.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by users at each pool's fee tier.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by users at each pool's fee tier.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol fee: each pool's share of the swap fee, read from the pool (1/4 on every pool since launch).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Half of the protocol fee, paid to the development fund.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Half of the protocol fee, sent to a fee jar that auctions it for GOO and burns the GOO.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Swap fees less the protocol fee, earned by liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Total swap volume on goo exchange pools.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees paid by users at each pool's fee tier.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees paid by users at each pool's fee tier.

Revenue.Swap Fees To GOO Buyback And Burn: Half of the protocol fee, sent to a fee jar that auctions it for GOO and burns the GOO.
Revenue.Swap Fees To Development Fund: Half of the protocol fee, paid to the development fund.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Development Fund: Half of the protocol fee, paid to the development fund.

HoldersRevenue.Swap Fees To GOO Buyback And Burn: Half of the protocol fee, sent to a fee jar that auctions it for GOO and burns the GOO.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees To LPs: Swap fees less the protocol fee, earned by liquidity providers.

methodology.Fees: Positive perpetual trading fees plus builder surcharges paid by users. Excludes funding payments and spot.
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus supply-side revenue. Because rebates and the MegaPop contribution accrue on their own rules, this is negative when they exceed fees collected in the window.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Fees going to treasury
methodology.HoldersRevenue: PopDEX does not buy back, burn, or distribute fees to token holders, so this is zero.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Maker rebates, referral rebates, the full builder surcharge, and MegaPop prize-pool contributions. Each is a share of trading fees accrued on its own rule, and is not capped by the fees collected in the same window.
methodology.Volume: Notional of perpetual taker fills, counted once, excluding spot.

Fees.Trading Fees: Positive perpetual trading fees paid by users.
Fees.Builder Fees: Builder surcharges paid by users on top of trading fees. The full amount is passed to the builder.

SupplySideRevenue.Builder Fees To Builders: Builder surcharges passed in full to the builder that routed the order.
SupplySideRevenue.Maker Rebates: Rebates paid to makers from the trading-fee split.
SupplySideRevenue.Referral Rebates: Rebates paid to referrers from the trading-fee split.
SupplySideRevenue.MegaPop Prize Pool Contributions: MegaPop prize-pool contributions taken from the trading-fee split and accrued by the MegaPop rules.

Revenue.Net Trading Fee Revenue: Trading fees left after rebates, builder surcharges, and the MegaPop contribution. Negative when those exceed fees collected in the window.

methodology.Fees: Trading fees on FAZE bonding curves and graduated pools, plus token launch and graduation fees. Settled fees are adjusted for opening and closing pending balances.
methodology.Revenue: Fees retained by FAZE: platform treasury allocations plus creator fees from FAZE own-token pools. Excludes other projects creator allocations and fees allocated to locked liquidity. Buybacks are a subsequent capital allocation, not additional revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator allocations for other launched tokens, including their own burners, plus fees allocated to locked liquidity. Pending allocations use the contracts live split at each boundary.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Retained revenue after reclassifying net fees paid to the FAZE buyback burner; includes FAZE own-pool creator fees not yet distributed. This is revenue attribution, not a treasury cash balance.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Native USDC fees paid by the hook to the designated FAZE buyback burner, less failed-payment recredits and actual keeper rewards. Recognized at funding rather than swap execution; excludes unrelated deposits and other tokens burners.

Fees.Curve Trading Fees: Actual fees charged in bonding-curve buy and sell events, in each launch quote asset.
Fees.Hook Trading Fees: Fees charged by the FAZE hook, recognized on accrual rather than when claimed; the pool LP fee is zero.
Fees.Token Launch Fees: Native USDC launch fee in force at the time of each launch, reconstructed from fee-setting events.
Fees.Graduation Fees: Quote-asset migration fee recorded on successful curve graduation.

Revenue.Fees Retained by FAZE: Gross fees less other-project creator allocations and locked-liquidity allocations; includes FAZE own-pool creator fees.

SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees to Creators: Fees allocated to creators of other tokens launched on FAZE, irrespective of whether they redirect them to their own burners.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees to Locked Liquidity: Trading fees allocated to compounding into locked positions, counted once at allocation.

ProtocolRevenue.FAZE Revenue After Buyback Funding: Total retained fee revenue less net fee-funded distributions to the FAZE burner. Funding can distribute prior-period earnings; negative periods are not clamped.

HoldersRevenue.FAZE Buyback Funding: Successful native fee payouts from hook OwedWithdrawn events to the FAZE burner, net of PayoutOwed recredits and keeper bountyWei. Unspent buyback funding remains included; executed spending is a separate measure.

methodology.Volume: Gross quote-asset volume on Loong bonding curves (buys at quoteIn, sells at quoteOut + fee + tax). Trading after graduation happens in PancakeSwap Infinity pools and is excluded here, as it belongs to PancakeSwap.
methodology.Fees: A 1% fee on every Loong trade, on the bonding curve and in graduated PancakeSwap Infinity pools (charged by the Loong hook), plus the launch-window anti-snipe tax (starts at 99% and decays to 0 over 3 seconds) and any token creation fee (currently 0).
methodology.Revenue: The 0.10% platform share and the 0.10% $LOONG buyback-and-burn share of every trade, plus token creation fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 0.10% platform share of every trade, plus token creation fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The 0.10% of every trade that funds $LOONG buybacks and burns; on the $LOONG coin itself its own 0.10% coin buyback-and-burn share also buys $LOONG.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 0.70% creator share of every trade, and the 0.10% used to buy back and burn the traded coin itself (except $LOONG).

Fees.Curve Trading Fees: CurveBuy and CurveSell fee + tax: the 1% trading fee plus any launch-window snipe tax (CurveBuy.fee already includes it).
Fees.Hook Trading Fees: HookFeeCollected feeAmount + taxAmount on graduated PancakeSwap Infinity pools, valued in the pool quote asset at the originating swap price when taken in the memecoin.
Fees.Token Creation Fees: Factory launchFee paid per TokenLaunched (0 BNB since deployment), replaying LaunchFeeUpdated changes in log order.

Revenue.Curve Fees To Loong: Platform share (10 of 100 bps) of bonding-curve fees.
Revenue.Hook Fees To Loong: Platform share (10 of 100 bps) of graduated-pool hook fees.
Revenue.Token Creation Fees To Loong: Token creation fees, paid to the protocol fee recipient.
Revenue.Curve Fees For LOONG Buyback And Burn: $LOONG vault share (10 of 100 bps) of bonding-curve fees, plus the coin buyback share on the $LOONG curve itself.
Revenue.Hook Fees For LOONG Buyback And Burn: $LOONG vault share (10 of 100 bps) of graduated-pool hook fees, plus the coin buyback share on the $LOONG pool itself.

ProtocolRevenue.Curve Fees To Loong: Platform share (10 of 100 bps) of bonding-curve fees.
ProtocolRevenue.Hook Fees To Loong: Platform share (10 of 100 bps) of graduated-pool hook fees.
ProtocolRevenue.Token Creation Fees To Loong: Token creation fees, paid to the protocol fee recipient.

HoldersRevenue.Curve Fees For LOONG Buyback And Burn: $LOONG vault share (10 of 100 bps) of bonding-curve fees, which the LoongBuybackBurner converts into $LOONG and burns; plus the coin buyback share on the $LOONG curve itself.
HoldersRevenue.Hook Fees For LOONG Buyback And Burn: $LOONG vault share (10 of 100 bps) of graduated-pool hook fees, which the LoongBuybackBurner converts into $LOONG and burns; plus the coin buyback share on the $LOONG pool itself.

SupplySideRevenue.Curve Fees To Creators: Creator share (70 of 100 bps) of bonding-curve fees, including rounding residue and any creator tax.
SupplySideRevenue.Hook Fees To Creators: Creator share (70 of 100 bps) of graduated-pool hook fees, including rounding residue and any creator tax.
SupplySideRevenue.Curve Fees For Meme Buybacks: Share (10 of 100 bps) of bonding-curve fees used to buy back and burn that launched coin.
SupplySideRevenue.Hook Fees For Meme Buybacks: Share (10 of 100 bps) of graduated-pool hook fees used to buy back and burn that launched coin.

methodology.Volume: Trading volume routed through the Kinetiq Markets interface's builder codes on Hyperliquid perps. Trades on Kinetiq's own HIP-3 markets are excluded here because Kinetiq Markets already counts them.
methodology.Fees: Builder-code fees paid by users trading on Hyperliquid through the Kinetiq Markets interface.
methodology.Revenue: Builder-code fees, retained entirely by Kinetiq.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue - retained by Kinetiq.

Fees.Hyperliquid Builder Code Fees: All perps trading fees using Hyperliquid builder code.

methodology.Volume: Swaps the Goo Exchange app routes through Nordstern on Robinhood Chain: Nordstern AggregatedTrade events whose transaction also carries the app's interface fee, paid by the trade's executor to the Goo Exchange treasury in the trade's output token. Transactions holding more than one Nordstern trade are skipped. The app's other outside routes (KyberSwap, LiquidSwap) can't be verified on-chain and are not counted; its own-pool route is DEX volume under Goo Exchange.
methodology.Fees: The app's 0.1% interface fee on its Nordstern routes (Nordstern encodes it in 1/65536 steps, so 0.0992%), taken from each trade's output. Fees paid in GOO are valued at the trade's own price.
methodology.UserFees: The app's 0.1% interface fee on its Nordstern routes, paid by the trader.
methodology.Revenue: All interface fees go to the Goo Exchange treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All interface fees go to the Goo Exchange treasury.

Fees.Interface Fees: The app's 0.1% interface fee on its Nordstern routes (Nordstern encodes it in 1/65536 steps, so 0.0992%), taken from each trade's output. Fees paid in GOO are valued at the trade's own price.

UserFees.Interface Fees: The app's 0.1% interface fee on its Nordstern routes, paid by the trader.

Revenue.Interface Fees To Treasury: All interface fees go to the Goo Exchange treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Interface Fees To Treasury: All interface fees go to the Goo Exchange treasury.

methodology.Volume: ETH traded on the moto.fun bonding curves (buys and sells before graduation).
methodology.Fees: Every bonding curve trade pays 1.20%: a 0.70% protocol fee to Motoswap and a 0.50% fee to the coin creator.
methodology.Revenue: The whole 0.70% protocol fee: the shares for MOTO stakers, MOTO buyback and burn, the treasury and the Rakeback program.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury share and the Rakeback program share of the 0.70% protocol fee.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of the 0.70% protocol fee paid to MOTO stakers plus the share used to buy back and burn MOTO.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 0.50% creator fee to coin creators.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: All bonding curve fees: the protocol fee (curve protocolFeeBps, 0.70% since launch) sent to the Motoswap Collector and the creator fee (curve creatorFeeBps, 0.50% since launch) accrued to the coin creator, from the Trade event.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: All bonding curve fees paid by traders: the protocol fee and the creator fee.

Revenue.Protocol Fees To MOTO Stakers: MOTO stakers bucket of the Collector (2/7 of the protocol fee since launch).
Revenue.Protocol Fees To MOTO Buyback And Burn: Buyback and burn bucket of the Collector (1/7 of the protocol fee since launch), used to buy MOTO and burn it.
Revenue.Protocol Fees To Treasury: Treasury bucket of the Collector (2/7 of the protocol fee since launch).
Revenue.Rakeback program: Rakeback bucket of the Collector (2/7 of the protocol fee since launch). Rakeback is a protocol-run program funded out of the protocol fee, so like token incentives it is spent from revenue, not a supply-side payment.

ProtocolRevenue.Protocol Fees To Treasury: Treasury bucket of the Collector (2/7 of the protocol fee since launch).
ProtocolRevenue.Rakeback program: Rakeback bucket of the Collector (2/7 of the protocol fee since launch). Rakeback is a protocol-run program funded out of the protocol fee, so like token incentives it is spent from revenue, not a supply-side payment.

HoldersRevenue.Protocol Fees To MOTO Stakers: MOTO stakers bucket of the Collector (2/7 of the protocol fee since launch).
HoldersRevenue.Protocol Fees To MOTO Buyback And Burn: Buyback and burn bucket of the Collector (1/7 of the protocol fee since launch), used to buy MOTO and burn it.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees To Coin Creators: Creator fee accrued to the coin creator in the CreatorFeeVault.

methodology.Fees: ORBIO creator and LP fees collected in harvests plus CREDIT order-book buyer fees swept by staking, excluding CREDIT activation burns and launchpad ORBIO fees.

Revenue.Rakeback program: Rakeback bucket of the Collector (2/7 of the protocol fee since launch). Rakeback is a protocol-run program funded out of the protocol fee, so like token incentives it is spent from revenue, not a supply-side payment.

ProtocolRevenue.Rakeback program: Rakeback bucket of the Collector (2/7 of the protocol fee since launch). Rakeback is a protocol-run program funded out of the protocol fee, so like token incentives it is spent from revenue, not a supply-side payment.

HoldersRevenue.Protocol Fees To MOTO Buyback And Burn: Buyback and burn bucket of the Collector (1/7 of the protocol fee since launch), used to buy MOTO and burn it.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees To Coin Creators: Creator fee accrued to the coin creator in the CreatorFeeVault.

methodology.Fees: Carriers pay XNET for mobile data offloaded onto WiFi. Until settlement arrives, Fees are conservatively accrued from measured daily offload. Closed unsettled months use XNET's official monthly projection and newer days use a conservative API-GB rate. Carrier payments typically settle about two months later, and historical accrual is reconciled to the amount actually paid.
methodology.Revenue: Carrier WiFi offload Fees retained within XNET after payments to operators that elect fiat compensation under XIP-13.1.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Passed XIP-13.1 lets designated operators choose fiat instead of token distributions. Their 75% operator cash share is Supply-Side Revenue and is attributed to the service month reconciled by the carrier settlement that funds the payout, preserving the observed NET60+ settlement cadence.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Accrued service-period tokenholder allocation. Historically 80% of ordinary carrier Fees accrued to buyback-and-burn; under passed XIP-12, 60% does. The XIP-13.1 fiat slice contributes its 5% facilitation/BBB allocation. Values are provisional wherever the underlying Fees are provisional and reconcile with settlement. This is accrual attribution; actual on-chain buyback or burn execution can occur later.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Historically 20% of ordinary carrier Fees was allocated to operations. Under passed XIP-12, Protocol Revenue is 40%: 20% operations and 20% protocol-owned liquidity. For the XIP-13.1 fiat slice, 20% is retained for XNET operations.

Fees.Carrier WiFi Offload Fees: Gross carrier WiFi offload service Fees. Daily values are shaped by network offload, use official monthly projections when available, and are reconciled to actual carrier settlement.

Revenue.Carrier WiFi Offload Fees Retained: Carrier WiFi offload Fees retained within XNET after subtracting XIP-13.1 fiat-operator payouts.

SupplySideRevenue.Carrier WiFi Offload Fees To Fiat Deploy: Fiat compensation to designated operators under passed XIP-13.1. The operator cash share is 75% of that operator's gross fiat service allocation.

HoldersRevenue.Accrued Buyback & Burn Allocation: Service-period buyback-and-burn allocation for ordinary carrier Fees: historically 80%, and 60% under passed XIP-12. It follows the same provisional-and-reconciled accrual basis as Fees.
HoldersRevenue.Fiat Facilitation BBB Allocation: XIP-13.1 facilitation/BBB allocation equal to 5% of the fiat operator's gross service allocation.

ProtocolRevenue.Operations: Operations allocation: 20% of ordinary carrier Fees, plus the 20% operations portion of any XIP-13.1 fiat-operator service allocation.
ProtocolRevenue.Protocol-owned liquidity: Under passed XIP-12, 20% of ordinary carrier Fees is allocated to protocol-owned liquidity.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: Trading fees sent to the CronusBurner contract, which buys CRONUS and burns it (since 2026-09-22).

methodology.UserFees: Users pay $0 for transactions. sFUEL (gas token) is obtained free from faucets and has no market value.
methodology.Fees: SKALE uses sFUEL (SKALE Fuel), a gas token distributed FREE via faucets. While transactions consume gas on-chain, sFUEL has $0 monetary value. User fees are $0.
methodology.Revenue: Network revenue comes from SKL token staking subscriptions by dApp developers, not from transaction fees. On-chain transaction fees are $0 as sFUEL is free.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol revenue is generated through SKL staking model where dApp developers stake tokens for network access. Transaction fees contribute $0 as sFUEL is valueless.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Validators/nodes are compensated through SKL staking rewards, not transaction fees. On-chain gas fees in sFUEL are $0.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: No sFUEL is burned or distributed as revenue since it has no value. Revenue model is entirely based on SKL token staking.
